records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: spoke ... saying: the opening of a new speech
decisions.reason: The usual opening of a speech of God to Moses, as in 1:1. This speech runs to the end of the chapter (verse 37).

records.heading: Be holy, because I am holy

records.source: דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־כָּל־עֲדַ֧ת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֥ אֲלֵהֶ֖ם קְדֹשִׁ֣ים תִּהְי֑וּ כִּ֣י קָד֔וֹשׁ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Speak to all [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel, and you will say to them, holy you will be, for holy [am] I, Yahweh your God.
pieces: "Speak to the whole congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'You must be holy, because I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, am holy.

L.2: "Speak to all the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and say to them, 'You shall be holy, for holy [am] I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.2: "Speak to all the people of the community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Tell them: 'You must be holy, because I am holy. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: you shall be holy, for I am holy: Israel is to share the character of the God who has made them his own
decisions.reason: This is the fullest form of a call that runs through Leviticus (11:44-45; 20:7, 26; compare 21:8). "Holy" first means set apart, belonging to God and marked off from what is common (10:10). Here it also has a moral content: the commands that follow, about parents, the poor, workers, the deaf and blind, courts, neighbors and outsiders, show what a holy people looks like in daily life, not only at the altar. The reason given is God himself. His people are to be like him because they belong to him, and he is the one who makes them holy (20:8; 22:32). Peter quotes these words to Christians (1 Peter 1:15-16).

decisions.choice: all the congregation of Israel: the whole people, not only the priests
decisions.reason: Most laws in Leviticus are given to Moses for "the sons of Israel" or for Aaron. This speech is addressed to the whole assembled people (compare 8:3), as fits laws that every household must keep.

decisions.choice: you shall be holy: a command, and also a promise of what Israel will be
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary future, used in Hebrew law for commands. It states what Israel must be and, with "I am holy" beside it, what God means them to become.

decisions.choice: because I am holy. I am the LORD your God.
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the LORD your God" in a sentence of its own so that the reason stays short. Literal keeps the Hebrew order, "for holy [am] I".

decisions.choice: the whole congregation (Balanced); all the people of the community (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 8:3, Readable uses the more common word "community".

records.source: אִ֣ישׁ אִמּ֤וֹ וְאָבִיו֙ תִּירָ֔אוּ וְאֶת־שַׁבְּתֹתַ֖י תִּשְׁמֹ֑רוּ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Each [one], his mother and his father you will fear, and my sabbaths you will keep; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: {{gender:Every one of you|Every man among you}} is to show reverence to mother and father, and you are to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.3: {{gender:Each one|Each man}}, his mother and his father you shall fear, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sabbaths you shall keep; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.3: {{gender:Each of you|Every man among you}} must treat your mother and father with deep respect. And keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: each one shall fear his mother and father: everyone is to treat their parents with awe and respect
decisions.reason: The word for "each one" is the word for a man, used here for every person, men and women alike, as the plural verb shows. "Fear" is the same verb used for fearing God (verses 14, 32) and the sanctuary (verse 30): a deep respect that shows itself in conduct. The command matches Exodus 20:12, which says "honor"; here the mother is named first. Cursing a parent is a capital crime (20:9).

decisions.choice: keep my sabbaths: the weekly day of rest, which belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: "My sabbaths" are the seventh days that the LORD claims as his own (23:3; Exodus 31:13). Respect for parents and the keeping of the Sabbath stand together, as in the Ten Commandments, at the head of the holiness laws. The command is repeated in verse 30.

decisions.choice: show reverence to (Balanced); treat with deep respect (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Fear" a parent does not mean be afraid of them. Balanced and Readable say what the fear consists of. Literal keeps "fear".

records.source: אַל־תִּפְנוּ֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֱלִילִ֔ים וֵֽאלֹהֵי֙ מַסֵּכָ֔ה לֹ֥א תַעֲשׂ֖וּ לָכֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Do not turn to the worthless [things], and gods of molten metal not you will make for yourselves; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: Do not turn aside to idols, and do not make yourselves gods of molten metal. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.4: Do not turn to the worthless idols, and gods of cast metal you shall not make for yourselves; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.4: Do not worship idols. Do not make statues of gods out of melted metal. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: the worthless idols: false gods, which are nothing
decisions.reason: The word means "nothings", things of no worth, and sounds like the ordinary word for God. Calling idols by it mocks them: they are empty, and those who turn to them gain nothing (26:1; Psalm 96:5; Isaiah 2:8, 18). Another scornful word for idols, used in 26:30, is linked with a word for dung. Both words name the images people bowed to and the gods those images stood for.

decisions.choice: gods of molten metal: images made by pouring melted metal into a mold
decisions.reason: The same words name the golden calf (Exodus 32:4, 8) and are forbidden in Exodus 34:17. Like verse 3, the verse repeats one of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:3-5).

decisions.choice: turn to: look to someone for help and give them loyalty
decisions.reason: To "turn to" a god is to seek it out and rely on it. Verse 31 uses the same verb for turning to mediums.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable says what turning to an idol means. Literal and Balanced keep the image of turning.

records.source: וְכִ֧י תִזְבְּח֛וּ זֶ֥בַח שְׁלָמִ֖ים לַיהוָ֑ה לִֽרְצֹנְכֶ֖ם תִּזְבָּחֻֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And when you sacrifice [a] sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh, for your acceptance you will sacrifice it.
pieces: When you sacrifice a peace offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, sacrifice it in the way that wins acceptance for you.

L.5: And when you sacrifice a sacrifice of peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you shall sacrifice it for your acceptance.

R.5: When you offer a peace offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, do it the right way, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will accept you.

decisions.choice: a sacrifice of peace offerings: the offering shared as a meal
decisions.reason: The offering of 3:1, whose fat is burned on the altar while the worshiper eats most of the meat (7:11-21).

decisions.choice: for your acceptance: so that God accepts the worshiper
decisions.reason: An offering made by the rules is accepted, and through it the one who brings it is accepted (1:3; 22:19, 29). Verses 6-8 give the rule that decides it here: the meat must be eaten within two days.

decisions.choice: do it the right way, so that he will accept you
decisions.reason: Readable says that acceptance depends on following the rules of verses 6-8, and names God as the one who accepts.

records.source: בְּי֧וֹם זִבְחֲכֶ֛ם יֵאָכֵ֖ל וּמִֽמָּחֳרָ֑ת וְהַנּוֹתָר֙ עַד־י֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י בָּאֵ֖שׁ יִשָּׂרֵֽף׃
records.gloss: On [the] day of your sacrifice it will be eaten, and on [the] next day, and the remainder until [the] third day with fire will be burned.
pieces: Eat it on the day of your sacrifice or on the following day, and burn with fire whatever is still left on the third day.

L.6: On the day of your sacrifice it shall be eaten, and on the next day; and what remains until the third day shall be burned with fire.

R.6: Eat the meat on the day you offer it or on the day after. If any is left on the third day, burn it up.

decisions.choice: on the day or the next day; burned on the third: a limit of two days for eating the meat
decisions.reason: The same rule is given for a peace offering made for a vow or as a freewill gift (7:16-17). A thanksgiving offering had to be eaten on the same day (7:15; 22:29-30). Meat that was holy was not to be kept until it spoiled.

records.source: וְאִ֛ם הֵאָכֹ֥ל יֵאָכֵ֖ל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י פִּגּ֥וּל ה֖וּא לֹ֥א יֵרָצֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And if indeed it is eaten on the third day, foul [meat] it [is]; not will it be accepted.
pieces: If any of it is eaten on the third day, it has become foul meat and will not be accepted.

L.7: And if it is eaten at all on the third day, it [is] foul; it will not be accepted.

R.7: If anyone eats some of it on the third day, the meat is spoiled. God will not accept the offering.

decisions.choice: foul: meat from a sacrifice that is kept too long and so becomes unfit
decisions.reason: The rare word names meat of an offering that has been left past its time (7:18; Isaiah 65:4; Ezekiel 4:14). It is not about the meat going bad but about the holy meal being broken by eating it too late.

decisions.choice: it will not be accepted: the offering does the worshiper no good
decisions.reason: Eating on the third day undoes the acceptance verse 5 speaks of. 7:18 says that the offering will not even be "counted" to the one who brought it.

decisions.choice: God will not accept the offering
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who accepts and makes "the offering" the subject.

records.source: וְאֹֽכְלָיו֙ עֲוֺנ֣וֹ יִשָּׂ֔א כִּֽי־אֶת־קֹ֥דֶשׁ יְהוָ֖ה חִלֵּ֑ל וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מֵעַמֶּֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And [those] eating it his iniquity he will bear, for the holy [thing] of Yahweh he has profaned, and will be cut off the person that from its kinspeople.
pieces: Anyone who eats it will bear the consequences of their guilt, because they have profaned what is holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That person must be cut off from the people.

L.8: And whoever eats it will bear his iniquity, for he has profaned the holy thing of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and that person will be cut off from his people.

R.8: Anyone who eats it will be guilty, because they have treated something holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as if it were not holy. That person must be removed from the people.

decisions.choice: bear his iniquity: carry the guilt and its punishment
decisions.reason: The phrase means to be held responsible for a wrong and to suffer what follows from it (5:1; 7:18; 17:16).

decisions.choice: profaned the holy thing: treated what belongs to God as common
decisions.reason: To profane is to take something set apart for God and use it as if it were ordinary (10:10; 22:2, 15). The meat of the peace offering is holy to the LORD; eating it outside the time he set treats it as common food. The same verb is used for profaning God's name (verse 12) and a daughter (verse 29).

decisions.choice: that person will be cut off from the people: removed from the people of God
decisions.reason: The penalty of being "cut off", as in 7:20.

decisions.choice: treated ... as if it were not holy
decisions.reason: Readable explains "profane". Literal and Balanced keep the word.

records.source: וּֽבְקֻצְרְכֶם֙ אֶת־קְצִ֣יר אַרְצְכֶ֔ם לֹ֧א תְכַלֶּ֛ה פְּאַ֥ת שָׂדְךָ֖ לִקְצֹ֑ר וְלֶ֥קֶט קְצִֽירְךָ֖ לֹ֥א תְלַקֵּֽט׃
records.gloss: And when you harvest the harvest of your land, not will you finish [the] edge of your field to harvest, and [the] gleaning of your harvest not will you gather.
pieces: When you gather in your land's harvest, do not cut the grain right up to the edges of your field, and do not collect what is left lying after the reapers.

L.9: And when you reap the harvest of your land, you shall not finish the edge of your field in reaping, and the gleaning of your harvest you shall not gather.

R.9: When you harvest the grain in your land, do not cut all of it, right to the edges of your field. And do not go back to pick up the grain that the workers dropped.

decisions.choice: the edge of your field: a strip of standing grain left uncut
decisions.reason: The owner was not to reap the whole field to its borders but to leave the corners and edges standing. The poor could then harvest it for themselves. The law is repeated in 23:22.

decisions.choice: the gleaning: stalks and ears dropped by the reapers
decisions.reason: Gleaning is what falls to the ground or is missed during the harvest. The poor followed the reapers to pick it up, as Ruth did in the fields of Boaz (Ruth 2:2-3, 15-17; compare Deuteronomy 24:19).

decisions.choice: cut the grain (Balanced); harvest the grain (Readable)
decisions.reason: The harvest in view is grain, as "field" and the gleaning show; verse 10 turns to the vineyard.

records.source: וְכַרְמְךָ֙ לֹ֣א תְעוֹלֵ֔ל וּפֶ֥רֶט כַּרְמְךָ֖ לֹ֣א תְלַקֵּ֑ט לֶֽעָנִ֤י וְלַגֵּר֙ תַּעֲזֹ֣ב אֹתָ֔ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And your vineyard not will you glean, and [the] fallen [grapes] of your vineyard not will you gather; for the poor and for the sojourner you will leave them; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: Do not go back through your vineyard to take every last cluster, or collect the grapes that drop to the ground. Leave them for the poor and for the outsider. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.10: And your vineyard you shall not glean, and the fallen [grapes] of your vineyard you shall not gather; for the poor and for the sojourner you shall leave them; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.10: Do not go through your vineyard a second time to pick every bunch of grapes. Do not pick up the grapes that fall on the ground. Leave them for poor people and for strangers. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: glean your vineyard; the fallen grapes: going over the vines again, and picking up dropped fruit
decisions.reason: The first verb means to go back over the vines for the small clusters left after the main picking (Deuteronomy 24:21; Judges 8:2). The second word names single grapes that fall during the harvest. Both are left for others.

decisions.choice: the sojourner: a person from outside Israel who lives among the people
decisions.reason: A sojourner was someone from another people or tribe who had settled in Israel, living there without land of their own or the protection of a family. Such people often depended on others' goodwill, and the law groups them with the poor, the fatherless and widows (23:22; Deuteronomy 24:19-21). Leviticus protects them (verses 33-34) and also holds them to many of Israel's laws (17:8-15; 24:22). Israel itself had been sojourners in Egypt (verse 34; Exodus 22:20).

decisions.choice: I am the LORD your God: the reason for the command
decisions.reason: The words, repeated through the chapter, ground each law in who God is (see 18:2). Here the harvest belongs to him, and he gives a share of it to those who have no field of their own (compare 25:23).

decisions.choice: outsider (Balanced); strangers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal says "sojourner", Balanced "outsider" and Readable "stranger", as in 17:8 and 25:23. All three describe a person living among a people not their own.

decisions.choice: go back through ... to take every last cluster (Balanced); go through ... a second time (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "glean your vineyard" involves.

records.source: לֹ֖א תִּגְנֹ֑בוּ וְלֹא־תְכַחֲשׁ֥וּ וְלֹֽא־תְשַׁקְּר֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲמִיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Not will you steal, and not will you deceive, and not will you deal falsely, [a] man with his fellow.
pieces: Do not steal, do not deny what you owe, and do not deal dishonestly with one another.

L.11: You shall not steal, and you shall not deceive, and you shall not deal falsely, each one with his fellow.

R.11: Do not steal. Do not lie about what you owe. Do not cheat each other.

decisions.choice: deceive ... deal falsely: deny the truth about what belongs to another, and act dishonestly
decisions.reason: The two verbs are the ones used in 5:21-22 for a person who denies having a neighbor's deposit or something he found, and swears falsely about it. Together with "steal" they forbid taking or keeping what is another's by force or by lying. Compare Exodus 20:15-16.

decisions.choice: a man with his fellow: with one another
decisions.reason: The phrase means "with each other". The word for fellow names a member of the same community (5:21; 25:14).

decisions.choice: deny what you owe (Balanced); lie about what you owe (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the verb the sense it has in 5:21-22. Literal keeps "deceive".

records.source: וְלֹֽא־תִשָּׁבְע֥וּ בִשְׁמִ֖י לַשָּׁ֑קֶר וְחִלַּלְתָּ֛ אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And not will you swear by my name to falsehood, and [so] you will profane [the] name of your God; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Do not take an oath in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name to back up a lie; that would profane the name of your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: And you shall not swear by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name falsely, and [so] profane the name of your God; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: Do not make a promise using {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name when you know it is false. That would dishonor the name of your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: swear by my name falsely: call on God as witness to what is not true
decisions.reason: An oath called on God to confirm a statement or a promise and to punish the one who broke it. To swear by his name to a lie makes him seem to stand behind it. Compare Exodus 20:7 and 5:22-24.

decisions.choice: profane the name of your God: treat his name as common and so dishonor him
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself. To use it for a lie is to treat it as ordinary (see verse 8), and so to dishonor him among the people (18:21; 20:3; 22:32).

decisions.choice: dishonor
decisions.reason: Readable says "dishonor" for "profane", as the plainest word for treating the name with disrespect.

records.source: לֹֽא־תַעֲשֹׁ֥ק אֶת־רֵֽעֲךָ֖ וְלֹ֣א תִגְזֹ֑ל לֹֽא־תָלִ֞ין פְּעֻלַּ֥ת שָׂכִ֛יר אִתְּךָ֖ עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: Not will you oppress your neighbor, and not will you rob [him]; not will remain overnight [the] wage of [a] hired laborer with you until morning.
pieces: Do not exploit your neighbor or take what is theirs by force. When you hire a laborer, the pay must not stay in your hands overnight until morning.

L.13: You shall not oppress your neighbor, and you shall not rob [him]; the wages of a hired laborer shall not remain with you overnight until morning.

R.13: Do not take advantage of your neighbor. Do not take what belongs to them. If you hire a worker, pay the worker the same day. Do not keep the pay until the next morning.

decisions.choice: oppress ... rob: take from another by power or by force
decisions.reason: The first verb means to wrong someone by using power over them, often by withholding what is due (Deuteronomy 24:14). The second is to seize something openly. Both appear in 5:21-23 among the wrongs that require a guilt offering.

decisions.choice: the wages of a hired laborer: pay owed to a day worker, due before night
decisions.reason: A hired laborer worked by the day and lived on what he earned. Deuteronomy 24:14-15 gives the reason: the worker is poor and is counting on it. To keep the wage overnight is a form of the oppression the verse forbids (Jeremiah 22:13; James 5:4).

decisions.choice: your neighbor: a fellow member of the community
decisions.reason: The word means a companion or fellow, anyone one has dealings with. Verses 16 and 18 use it again; see the note on verse 18.

decisions.choice: pay the worker the same day. Do not keep the pay until the next morning.
decisions.reason: Readable states the command positively and then gives the Hebrew prohibition.

records.source: לֹא־תְקַלֵּ֣ל חֵרֵ֔שׁ וְלִפְנֵ֣י עִוֵּ֔ר לֹ֥א תִתֵּ֖ן מִכְשֹׁ֑ל וְיָרֵ֥אתָ מֵּאֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not will you curse [a] deaf [person], and before [a] blind [person] not will you put [a] stumbling block, and you will fear [from] your God; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Do not curse someone who is deaf, and do not set something in the path of someone who is blind to make them trip. Fear your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: You shall not curse the deaf, and before the blind you shall not put a stumbling block; and you shall fear your God; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: Do not say evil things about a deaf person. Do not put something in front of a blind person to make them fall. Have respect for your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the deaf, the blind, and the fear of God: God sees the wrongs that their victims cannot
decisions.reason: A deaf person cannot hear the curse and a blind person cannot see the obstacle, so no one could bring a charge. The command to fear God answers that: he hears and sees, and he will hold the wrongdoer to account (verse 32; 25:17; Deuteronomy 27:18).

decisions.choice: stumbling block: anything that makes someone trip and fall
decisions.reason: The word means an object one trips over. Later it is used for whatever leads someone into sin or ruin (Ezekiel 14:3; compare Romans 14:13), but here the plain sense is meant.

decisions.choice: say evil things about (Readable); have respect for (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "curse" and gives "fear your God" the sense of awe and respect, as in 25:17. Literal and Balanced keep "curse" and "fear".

records.source: לֹא־תַעֲשׂ֥וּ עָ֨וֶל֙ בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט לֹא־תִשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי־דָ֔ל וְלֹ֥א תֶהְדַּ֖ר פְּנֵ֣י גָד֑וֹל בְּצֶ֖דֶק תִּשְׁפֹּ֥ט עֲמִיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Not will you do injustice in judgment; not will you lift up [the] face of [a] poor [person], and not will you honor [the] face of [a] great [person]; in righteousness you will judge your fellow.
pieces: Do not do wrong when you judge a case. Do not take the side of the poor because they are poor, and do not give special honor to the powerful. Judge your fellow citizen fairly.

L.15: You shall not do injustice in judgment; you shall not lift up the face of the poor, and you shall not honor the face of the great; in righteousness you shall judge your fellow.

R.15: When you judge, do what is right. Do not favor poor people because you feel sorry for them. Do not favor important people because they have power. Be fair when you judge others.

decisions.choice: lift up the face of the poor; honor the face of the great: favor someone because of who they are
decisions.reason: To "lift the face" of a person is to show them favor, here in court. The judge must not favor the poor out of pity or the great out of respect or fear, but decide by what is right (Exodus 23:3, 6; Deuteronomy 1:17; 16:19).

decisions.choice: in righteousness: by what is right, fairly
decisions.reason: The word means what is right and just, measured by God's standard. A judgment "in righteousness" is one that gives each person what is due. Verse 36 uses the same word for honest scales and weights.

decisions.choice: fairly (Balanced); be fair (Readable)
decisions.reason: In a court "in righteousness" means fairly. Literal keeps "in righteousness".

decisions.choice: because you feel sorry for them ... because they have power
decisions.reason: Readable supplies the reasons a judge might be tempted to favor each one, which the context implies.

records.source: לֹא־תֵלֵ֤ךְ רָכִיל֙ בְּעַמֶּ֔יךָ לֹ֥א תַעֲמֹ֖ד עַל־דַּ֣ם רֵעֶ֑ךָ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not will you go about [as a] slanderer among your kinspeople; not will you stand against [the] blood of your neighbor; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Do not go from one person to another spreading slander among your people. Do not take a stand against your neighbor's life. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.16: You shall not go about [as] a slanderer among your people; you shall not stand against the blood of your neighbor; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.16: Do not go around telling lies about people. Do not do anything that could cost your neighbor's life. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: go about as a slanderer: spread damaging talk about others
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb for going about as a trader, and names a person who carries stories from one to another to harm someone (Proverbs 11:13; 20:19; Jeremiah 9:3; Ezekiel 22:9).

decisions.choice: stand against the blood of your neighbor: act in a way that puts your neighbor's life at risk
alternatives: do not stand idly by while your neighbor's life is in danger
decisions.reason: The phrase is found only here. Next to slander, it most likely means to speak or act against someone so that his life is at stake, as a false witness might in court (1 Kings 21:10-13; Ezekiel 22:9). Another reading is "do not stand by while your neighbor's blood is shed", that is, do not hold back from saving him. Both readings forbid seeking or allowing a neighbor's death for one's own gain.

decisions.choice: life
decisions.reason: "Blood" here stands for a person's life. Literal keeps "blood".

records.source: לֹֽא־תִשְׂנָ֥א אֶת־אָחִ֖יךָ בִּלְבָבֶ֑ךָ הוֹכֵ֤חַ תּוֹכִ֨יחַ֙ אֶת־עֲמִיתֶ֔ךָ וְלֹא־תִשָּׂ֥א עָלָ֖יו חֵֽטְא׃
records.gloss: Not will you hate your brother in your heart; surely you will rebuke your fellow, and not will you bear on account of him sin.
pieces: Do not hold hatred in your heart for one of your own people. Be sure to correct your neighbor when they do wrong, so that you do not carry sin because of them.

L.17: You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall surely rebuke your fellow, and you shall not bear sin because of him.

R.17: Do not secretly hate any of your people. If your neighbor does wrong, tell them plainly. Then you will not be guilty because of their sin.

decisions.choice: your brother: a fellow Israelite
decisions.reason: "Brother" here means any member of the people, as often in the law (25:25, 35; Deuteronomy 15:7). The parallel words in this verse and the next are "fellow", "the sons of your people" and "neighbor".

decisions.choice: you shall surely rebuke: speak openly to the one who has done wrong
decisions.reason: The doubled verb stresses the command. Instead of hating in silence, the wronged person is to correct the wrongdoer openly. The verse sets hidden hatred against frank rebuke (Proverbs 27:5; Matthew 18:15).

decisions.choice: not bear sin because of him: not take on guilt on account of the other person
alternatives: and you will not lay sin on him
decisions.reason: The words may mean that one who stays silent shares the guilt of the wrongdoer (Ezekiel 3:18-21), or that hatred kept in the heart becomes one's own sin. They could also be read "and not lay sin on him", that is, not burden him with blame. The reading "because of him" fits the use of the same phrase in 22:9 and Numbers 18:32.

decisions.choice: one of your own people
decisions.reason: "Brother" means a fellow Israelite here, so Balanced says "one of your own people" and Readable "any of your people". Literal keeps "brother".

decisions.choice: when they do wrong (Balanced); if your neighbor does wrong (Readable)
decisions.reason: The rebuke assumes a wrong has been done. Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: לֹֽא־תִקֹּ֤ם וְלֹֽא־תִטֹּר֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְאָֽהַבְתָּ֥ לְרֵעֲךָ֖ כָּמ֑וֹךָ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not will you avenge [yourself], and not will you keep [anger] against [the] sons of your people, and you will love your neighbor as yourself; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Do not pay back any of your own people with revenge, and do not keep holding a grudge against them. Instead, love your neighbor as yourself. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.18: You shall not take vengeance, and you shall not keep [anger] against the {{gender:children|sons}} of your people, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.18: Do not try to get even with any of your people. Do not stay angry at them. Love your neighbor as much as you love yourself. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: love your neighbor as yourself: seek your neighbor's good as you seek your own
decisions.reason: The command sums up the laws around it. In verses 11-18 the "neighbor" is a fellow member of the people, and loving him means not cheating, robbing, slandering, hating or taking revenge on him, and correcting him openly. Love here is not only a feeling but a way of acting, measured by the care one already gives oneself. Verse 34 gives the same command for the outsider who lives in the land. Jesus names it the second great commandment, after loving God (Deuteronomy 6:5), in Matthew 22:39 (also Matthew 19:19; Mark 12:31), and when he is asked "who is my neighbor?" he answers with the parable of the Samaritan (Luke 10:27-37). Paul says the whole law is summed up in it (Romans 13:9; Galatians 5:14), and James calls it "the royal law" (James 2:8).

decisions.choice: take vengeance; keep anger: pay back a wrong, or nurse resentment over it
decisions.reason: The first verb means to avenge oneself. The second means to keep or guard; with no object it means to keep anger alive, to bear a grudge (Psalm 103:9; Jeremiah 3:5, 12; Nahum 1:2, where it is said of God). The laws forbid both the act of revenge and the resentment that leads to it. Vengeance belongs to God (Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19).

decisions.choice: love your neighbor: the verb takes an unusual preposition before "neighbor"
decisions.reason: Hebrew usually puts "love" directly before its object, but here (and in verse 34) a small word for "to" or "for" stands between. It may stress acting for the neighbor's good. The meaning "love your neighbor" is not in doubt.

decisions.choice: keep holding a grudge (Balanced); stay angry (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb "keep" has no object; Balanced and Readable supply what is kept. Literal supplies [anger] in brackets.

decisions.choice: as much as you love yourself
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the comparison "as yourself".

records.source: אֶֽת־חֻקֹּתַי֮ תִּשְׁמֹרוּ֒ בְּהֶמְתְּךָ֙ לֹא־תַרְבִּ֣יעַ כִּלְאַ֔יִם שָׂדְךָ֖ לֹא־תִזְרַ֣ע כִּלְאָ֑יִם וּבֶ֤גֶד כִּלְאַ֨יִם֙ שַֽׁעַטְנֵ֔ז לֹ֥א יַעֲלֶ֖ה עָלֶֽיךָ׃פ
records.gloss: My statutes you will keep; your livestock not will you make lie [with] two kinds; your field not will you sow [with] two kinds; and [a] garment of two kinds, mixed stuff, not will come up on you.
pieces: Keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes. Do not let two different kinds of your animals breed together. Do not sow your field with two kinds of seed. Do not put on clothing made from two kinds of thread mixed together.

L.19: You shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes. Your livestock you shall not make breed [with] two kinds; your field you shall not sow [with] two kinds; and a garment of two kinds, mixed stuff, shall not come upon you.

R.19: Obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws. Do not let two different kinds of animals mate. Do not plant two kinds of seed in the same field. Do not wear clothes woven from two different kinds of thread.

decisions.choice: two kinds: mixing what God made distinct
decisions.reason: Animals are not to be bred with another kind, nor a field sown with two kinds of seed (Deuteronomy 22:9-11 adds yoking an ox with a donkey). In the creation account each living thing is made "according to its kind" (Genesis 1:11-12, 21, 24-25). These laws keep the kinds apart as God made them, as the holy people is kept distinct from the nations (20:24-26).

decisions.choice: a garment of two kinds, mixed stuff: cloth woven of wool and linen together
decisions.reason: The rare word is explained in Deuteronomy 22:11: "wool and linen together". Some parts of the priests' clothing and of the tabernacle's curtains were made of such mixed weaving (Exodus 26:1; 28:6; 39:29), so the mixture may have been kept for holy things.

decisions.choice: my statutes: the fixed rules God has laid down
decisions.reason: The word for statutes (see 18:4) introduces laws whose reason is not given, as these are.

decisions.choice: laws
decisions.reason: Readable says "laws" for "statutes", as in the settled wording for this word.

records.source: וְ֠אִישׁ כִּֽי־יִשְׁכַּ֨ב אֶת־אִשָּׁ֜ה שִׁכְבַת־זֶ֗רַע וְהִ֤וא שִׁפְחָה֙ נֶחֱרֶ֣פֶת לְאִ֔ישׁ וְהָפְדֵּה֙ לֹ֣א נִפְדָּ֔תָה א֥וֹ חֻפְשָׁ֖ה לֹ֣א נִתַּן־לָ֑הּ בִּקֹּ֧רֶת תִּהְיֶ֛ה לֹ֥א יוּמְת֖וּ כִּי־לֹ֥א חֻפָּֽשָׁה׃
records.gloss: And [a] man, when he lies with [a] woman [a] lying of seed, and she [is a] female slave assigned to [a] man, and indeed not she has been redeemed, or freedom not has been given to her, compensation there will be; not will they be put to death, for not she had been freed.
pieces: If a man has sexual relations with a woman who is a slave promised to another man, and she has not been bought back or given her freedom, compensation must be paid. They are not to be put to death, since she was not free.

L.20: And if a man lies with a woman [with] a lying of seed, and she [is] a slave woman assigned to a man, and she has not at all been redeemed, or freedom has not been given to her, there shall be compensation; they shall not be put to death, for she had not been freed.

R.20: Suppose a man has sex with a woman who is a slave. She has been promised to another man, but no one has paid to free her, and she has not been set free. Then a payment must be made for the wrong. But the man and the woman must not be put to death, because she was not free.

decisions.choice: a slave woman assigned to a man: a slave already pledged to another man as his wife
decisions.reason: The verb is used only here and means designated or set aside. The woman is betrothed but still a slave. Had she been free, the act would be adultery with a betrothed woman, for which both would die (20:10; Deuteronomy 22:23-24). Because she is not free, the betrothal does not count as a full marriage, and the death penalty does not apply.

decisions.choice: compensation: the word is rare and its sense uncertain
decisions.reason: The word appears only here. It comes from a root meaning to examine or seek out. It may mean that damages are paid (most likely to the man to whom she was promised, as the guilt offering of verses 21-22 suggests), that an inquiry is to be held, or that there will be punishment short of death.

decisions.choice: lies with a woman a lying of seed: has sexual intercourse with her
decisions.reason: The phrase is the one used in 15:18 and Numbers 5:13 for sexual intercourse.

decisions.choice: bought back (Balanced); paid to free her (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Redeemed" means bought out of slavery. Literal keeps "redeemed".

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are bought, sold, owned or released: she has not been bought back or freed, and the ruling turns on her not being free (m1).

records.heading: A slave woman promised to another man

records.source: וְהֵבִ֤יא אֶת־אֲשָׁמוֹ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד אֵ֖יל אָשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And he will bring his guilt offering to Yahweh to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting, [a] ram of guilt offering.
pieces: The man is to bring a ram to the entrance of the tent of meeting as his guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: And he shall bring his guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram [as] a guilt offering.

R.21: The man must bring a ram to the entrance of the meeting tent. It will be his guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: guilt offering: the offering that makes amends for a wrong
decisions.reason: The offering of 5:14-26, brought when someone has wronged what belongs to God or to another person. Here the man has wronged the man to whom the slave woman was promised, and through him has broken faith with God. See the note at 5:15.

decisions.choice: The man
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he". Balanced and Readable name the man, since the woman of verse 20 brings nothing.

records.source: וְכִפֶּר֩ עָלָ֨יו הַכֹּהֵ֜ן בְּאֵ֤יל הָֽאָשָׁם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עַל־חַטָּאת֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֑א וְנִסְלַ֣ח ל֔וֹ מֵחַטָּאת֖וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָֽא׃פ
records.gloss: And will make atonement for him the priest with [the] ram of the guilt offering before Yahweh for his sin which he has sinned, and it will be forgiven to him, from his sin which he has sinned.
pieces: With the ram of the guilt offering the priest is to make atonement for him before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for the sin he committed, and he will be forgiven for that sin.

L.22: And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for his sin which he has sinned, and it will be forgiven him, from his sin which he has sinned.

R.22: The priest will use the ram of the guilt offering to make atonement for the man before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He will make atonement for the sin the man did, and the man will be forgiven.

decisions.choice: make atonement ... it will be forgiven him: the wrong is dealt with and the man is forgiven
decisions.reason: As in 4:20 and 5:16, the priest's work of atonement leads to God's forgiveness. See 1:4 on atonement.

records.source: וְכִי־תָבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־הָאָ֗רֶץ וּנְטַעְתֶּם֙ כָּל־עֵ֣ץ מַאֲכָ֔ל וַעֲרַלְתֶּ֥ם עָרְלָת֖וֹ אֶת־פִּרְי֑וֹ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֗ים יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם עֲרֵלִ֖ים לֹ֥א יֵאָכֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And when you come into the land and you plant every tree of food, and you will count as foreskin its foreskin, its fruit; three years it will be to you uncircumcised; not will it be eaten.
pieces: When you enter the land and plant any tree that bears food, you are to regard its fruit as uncircumcised. For three years it will be uncircumcised for you, and none of it may be eaten.

L.23: And when you come into the land and plant any tree for food, you shall count its fruit [as] its foreskin; three years it shall be uncircumcised to you; it shall not be eaten.

R.23: When you go into the land, you will plant all kinds of fruit trees. For the first three years, treat their fruit as forbidden. Do not eat any of it.

decisions.choice: count its fruit as its foreskin; uncircumcised: the fruit of the first years is not yet fit for use
decisions.reason: The picture is of circumcision. Just as a boy was not counted among the covenant people until he was circumcised (12:3), a young tree's fruit is set aside as "uncircumcised" and not used. The same image is used for lips and hearts that are not ready to serve God (Exodus 6:12; 26:41).

decisions.choice: three years: the tree's first fruit is left unpicked
decisions.reason: For three years the fruit is not eaten; in the fourth it is given to God (verse 24), and only from the fifth is it eaten (verse 25). Fruit trees in the land, like the firstborn and the first of the harvest, are first acknowledged as God's gift (Exodus 23:19).

decisions.choice: forbidden
decisions.reason: Readable says what "uncircumcised" means here, that the fruit may not be used. Literal and Balanced keep the image.

records.heading: Fruit trees, mourning and other laws

records.source: וּבַשָּׁנָה֙ הָרְבִיעִ֔ת יִהְיֶ֖ה כָּל־פִּרְי֑וֹ קֹ֥דֶשׁ הִלּוּלִ֖ים לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And in the fourth year will be all its fruit holy, [an offering] of praise to Yahweh.
pieces: In the fourth year all its fruit is to be set apart as holy, given in praise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.24: And in the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, [an offering] of praises to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.24: In the fourth year, all the fruit will be holy. Give it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: holy, of praises: the whole crop is given to God with thanksgiving
decisions.reason: The fruit of the fourth year belongs to God. The word for praise is used of the joyful festival at harvest in Judges 9:27. How the fruit was given is not said; it may have been eaten before the LORD at the sanctuary, as the second tithe was (Deuteronomy 14:22-26), or given to the priests (Numbers 18:12-13).

records.source: וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֗ת תֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ אֶת־פִּרְי֔וֹ לְהוֹסִ֥יף לָכֶ֖ם תְּבוּאָת֑וֹ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And in the fifth year you will eat its fruit, to add to you its produce; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: From the fifth year on you may eat its fruit. Doing this will make the tree yield more for you. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.25: And in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, to increase its produce for you; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.25: Then, in the fifth year, you may eat the fruit. If you obey this rule, your trees will give you more fruit. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: to increase its produce for you: the waiting leads to a greater harvest
decisions.reason: The words give the result of obeying the law: by waiting and giving the first fruit to God, Israel will have more fruit. It is God who gives the increase (compare 25:21; 26:4).

decisions.choice: Doing this will make (Balanced); If you obey this rule (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "to add". Balanced and Readable say that it is keeping the law of verses 23-25 that leads to the increase.

records.source: לֹ֥א תֹאכְל֖וּ עַל־הַדָּ֑ם לֹ֥א תְנַחֲשׁ֖וּ וְלֹ֥א תְעוֹנֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: Not will you eat with the blood; not will you practice divination, and not will you practice soothsaying.
pieces: Do not eat anything with its blood still in it. Do not try to read the future, whether by divining or by soothsaying.

L.26: You shall not eat with the blood; you shall not practice divination and you shall not practice soothsaying.

R.26: Do not eat meat that still has blood in it. Do not use magic to find out what will happen in the future.

decisions.choice: eat with the blood: eat meat that still has its blood in it
alternatives: do not eat beside the blood (in a pagan rite)
do not eat on the mountains (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean eating meat that has not been drained of blood, which 17:10-14 forbids (Genesis 9:4; 1 Samuel 14:32-34, where the same wording is used). Some take them to mean eating beside the blood poured out as part of a pagan rite, which would fit the ban on divination that follows. The Septuagint reads "on the mountains", a different text.

decisions.choice: practice divination; soothsaying: ways of trying to learn the future by signs or magic
decisions.reason: The first verb may refer to reading omens, as in Genesis 44:5, 15. The second is of uncertain origin; it may mean reading the clouds or a form of fortune-telling (Deuteronomy 18:10, 14; 2 Kings 21:6). Israel was to seek God's will through his word and his prophets, not by such means (Deuteronomy 18:9-15).

decisions.choice: use magic to find out what will happen
decisions.reason: Readable names both practices together by what they aim to do. Literal and Balanced keep the two terms.

records.source: לֹ֣א תַקִּ֔פוּ פְּאַ֖ת רֹאשְׁכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֣א תַשְׁחִ֔ית אֵ֖ת פְּאַ֥ת זְקָנֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Not will you round off [the] edge of your head, and not will you destroy [the] edge of your beard.
pieces: Do not shave off the hair around the sides of your head, and do not cut away the corners of your beard.

L.27: You shall not round off the edge of your head, and you shall not destroy the edge of your beard.

R.27: Do not cut the hair on the sides of your head short all around. Do not cut off the edges of your beard.

decisions.choice: round off the edge of your head; destroy the edge of your beard: cutting hair and beard as other peoples did
decisions.reason: The sides of the head are the hair at the temples and above the ears. Shaving the head round and cutting the beard were signs of mourning among the nations (Jeremiah 9:25; 48:37; compare Deuteronomy 14:1), and perhaps also marks of devotion to their gods. The priests receive the same rule in 21:5. With verse 28, the verse forbids marking the body in mourning as the nations did.

records.source: וְשֶׂ֣רֶט לָנֶ֗פֶשׁ לֹ֤א תִתְּנוּ֙ בִּבְשַׂרְכֶ֔ם וּכְתֹ֣בֶת קַֽעֲקַ֔ע לֹ֥א תִתְּנ֖וּ בָּכֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And cut[s] for [the] dead not will you make in your flesh, and [the] writing of [an] incision not will you make on yourselves; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Do not gash your flesh in mourning for the dead, and do not mark your skin with tattoos. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.28: And cuts for the dead you shall not make in your flesh, and marks of tattooing you shall not put on yourselves; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.28: When someone dies, do not cut your body to show your sorrow. Do not put tattoos on your skin. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: cuts for the dead: gashing the body as a rite of mourning
decisions.reason: The word for "the dead" is the word for a person or soul, used here of a dead person (as in 21:1). Cutting oneself was part of mourning (Jeremiah 16:6; 41:5) and of pagan worship (1 Kings 18:28). Israel belongs to God and is not to mourn this way (Deuteronomy 14:1-2).

decisions.choice: the writing of an incision: a mark cut or pricked into the skin
decisions.reason: The second word is found only here. Together the words probably describe a tattoo, a design put into the skin. What kind of mark it was, and whether it was linked with mourning or with devotion to a god, is not said.

decisions.choice: in mourning (Balanced); to show your sorrow (Readable)
decisions.reason: The cuts are "for the dead", so Balanced and Readable say that they are a sign of grief.

records.source: אַל־תְּחַלֵּ֥ל אֶֽת־בִּתְּךָ֖ לְהַזְנוֹתָ֑הּ וְלֹא־תִזְנֶ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמָלְאָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ זִמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, and [so] not will prostitute itself the land, and will be full the land [of] wickedness.
pieces: Do not dishonor your daughter by giving her over to prostitution, or the land will prostitute itself and fill up with lewd wickedness.

L.29: Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, so that the land does not prostitute itself and the land become full of wickedness.

R.29: Do not make your daughter a prostitute. That would bring shame on her. If you do this, the whole land will turn to sexual sin and be full of evil.

decisions.choice: profane your daughter by making her a prostitute: degrade her by selling her for sex
decisions.reason: A father had charge of his daughter until her marriage. To make her a prostitute is to treat her as common, robbing her of the honor that belongs to a daughter of God's holy people (compare 21:9). The verse may have in view prostitution linked with pagan worship (Deuteronomy 23:18), but it does not say so.

decisions.choice: the land will prostitute itself and be full of wickedness: the sin spreads until the whole land is corrupt
decisions.reason: The land itself is pictured as becoming unfaithful. The word translated wickedness is used for shameful sexual sin (18:17; 20:14). In 18:25-28 the land is defiled by such sins and vomits out its people.

decisions.choice: dishonor (Balanced); bring shame on (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "profane" when used of a person. Literal keeps "profane".

records.source: אֶת־שַׁבְּתֹתַ֣י תִּשְׁמֹ֔רוּ וּמִקְדָּשִׁ֖י תִּירָ֑אוּ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: My sabbaths you will keep, and my sanctuary you will fear; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: You are to keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbaths and stand in awe of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.30: You shall keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sabbaths, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary you shall fear; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.30: Keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Sabbath days, and respect {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sanctuary. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: my sanctuary: the holy place where the LORD dwells among his people
decisions.reason: The word means a holy place, a place set apart for God. Here it is the tent of meeting with its courtyard, where God lives among Israel (Exodus 25:8, "let them make me a sanctuary, so that I may dwell among them"). Later the same word is used for the temple. It is "my sanctuary" because it belongs to the LORD; it must not be defiled by uncleanness or by sin (15:31; 20:3; 21:12, 23).

decisions.choice: fear my sanctuary: treat the place of God's presence with reverent awe
decisions.reason: "Fear" here is not terror but the awe that guards how one comes near to God, keeping his rules for the holy place (10:1-3; 16:2). It is the same verb used for parents in verse 3 and for God in verses 14 and 32. The verse is repeated in 26:2.

decisions.choice: stand in awe of (Balanced); respect (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 26:2. Literal keeps "fear".

records.source: אַל־תִּפְנ֤וּ אֶל־הָאֹבֹת֙ וְאֶל־הַיִּדְּעֹנִ֔ים אַל־תְּבַקְשׁ֖וּ לְטָמְאָ֣ה בָהֶ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Do not turn to the mediums and to the spiritists; do not seek [them], to become unclean by them; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: Do not consult mediums or spiritists. Do not seek their help, or you will become unclean through them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.31: Do not turn to the mediums and to the spiritists; do not seek [them], to become unclean by them; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.31: Do not go to people who say they can talk with the dead or with spirits. Do not ask them for help. They will make you unclean. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: mediums and spiritists: people who claimed to call up the dead and learn from them
decisions.reason: The first word may name the spirit of a dead person, or the pit through which it was called up, or the one who called it (1 Samuel 28:7-8, where Saul visits such a woman at Endor; Isaiah 8:19; 29:4). The second comes from the verb "know" and names one who claims secret knowledge from the spirits. The two are always named together (20:6, 27; Deuteronomy 18:11; 2 Kings 21:6). Consulting them is a capital crime in 20:6 and 20:27.

decisions.choice: seek them, to become unclean: to turn to the dead for guidance makes one unclean
decisions.reason: Israel was to seek guidance from the living God (Isaiah 8:19-20). Turning instead to the dead is unfaithfulness to him, and it makes the one who does it unclean, unfit to come near God.

decisions.choice: people who say they can talk with the dead or with spirits
decisions.reason: Readable describes what mediums and spiritists claimed to do.

records.source: מִפְּנֵ֤י שֵׂיבָה֙ תָּק֔וּם וְהָדַרְתָּ֖ פְּנֵ֣י זָקֵ֑ן וְיָרֵ֥אתָ מֵּאֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: Before gray hair you will rise, and you will honor [the] face of [an] old [person], and you will fear [from] your God; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Rise to your feet in the presence of the gray-haired, and give honor to the old. Fear your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.32: Before the gray head you shall rise, and you shall honor the face of the old, and you shall fear your God; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.32: Stand up when an old person comes near, and show respect to people who are old. Have respect for your God. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: rise before the gray head: stand up to show honor to the aged
decisions.reason: Gray hair stands for old age, which was counted a crown of honor (Proverbs 16:31; 20:29). Rising when an older person came was a sign of respect (Job 29:8).

decisions.choice: fear your God: honoring the old is part of revering God
decisions.reason: As in verse 14, the fear of God stands behind the command. To honor the old is to honor the God who gives long life.

decisions.choice: the old (Balanced); people who are old (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means an old person; it is used here of the aged in general, women as well as men. Literal keeps "the old".

records.source: וְכִֽי־יָג֧וּר אִתְּךָ֛ גֵּ֖ר בְּאַרְצְכֶ֑ם לֹ֥א תוֹנ֖וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And when sojourns with you [a] sojourner in your land, not will you mistreat him.
pieces: If an outsider comes to live among you in your land, you are not to take advantage of them.

L.33: And when a sojourner sojourns with you in your land, you shall not mistreat him.

R.33: Sometimes a stranger will come to live with you in your land. Do not treat that person badly.

decisions.choice: a sojourner sojourns with you: an outsider settles among Israel
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun come from the same root: to live as an outsider in a land not one's own. See the note on the sojourner at verse 10.

decisions.choice: mistreat: oppress or take advantage of someone without protection
decisions.reason: The verb means to wrong someone, often by cheating or exploiting them (25:14, 17; Exodus 22:20; Ezekiel 22:7, 29). Without land or family, the outsider was easy to cheat.

records.heading: Love the outsider and keep honest measures

records.source: כְּאֶזְרָ֣ח מִכֶּם֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם הַגֵּ֣ר׀הַגָּ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֗ם וְאָהַבְתָּ֥ לוֹ֙ כָּמ֔וֹךָ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Like [a] native among you will be to you the sojourner who sojourns with you, and you will love him as yourself, for sojourners you were in [the] land of Egypt; I [am] Yahweh your God.
pieces: The outsider living among you is to count as one of your own native-born. You are to love them as yourself, since you yourselves were outsiders in the land of Egypt. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

L.34: Like a native among you shall be to you the sojourner who sojourns with you, and you shall love him as yourself, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.34: Treat strangers who live with you like people who were born in Israel. Love them as much as you love yourself. Remember that you were strangers in Egypt. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

decisions.choice: love him as yourself: the command of verse 18 extended to the outsider
decisions.reason: Verse 18 told Israel to love the neighbor, a fellow Israelite, as oneself. Here the same words are used of the outsider. The love owed to one's own people is owed also to the one from outside. Deuteronomy 10:18-19 says that God himself loves the sojourner, and Israel must too. Jesus' parable of the Samaritan makes the same point about who counts as a neighbor (Luke 10:29-37).

decisions.choice: like a native among you: with the same standing and the same justice as one born in Israel
decisions.reason: The native-born is an Israelite by birth (16:29; 17:15). The outsider is to receive the same treatment and the same law (24:22; Numbers 15:15-16).

decisions.choice: for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt: Israel's own past is the reason
decisions.reason: Israel lived as outsiders in Egypt and was oppressed there (Exodus 1:11-14; 22:20; 23:9). Remembering that, they are to treat outsiders as they wished to be treated.

decisions.choice: Remember that
decisions.reason: Readable turns the reason into a command to remember, as Deuteronomy often does (Deuteronomy 24:18, 22).

records.source: לֹא־תַעֲשׂ֥וּ עָ֖וֶל בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט בַּמִּדָּ֕ה בַּמִּשְׁקָ֖ל וּבַמְּשׂוּרָֽה׃
records.gloss: Not will you do injustice in judgment, in measurement, in weight, and in measure of volume.
pieces: Do not act unjustly when you decide cases, or when you measure length, weight or volume.

L.35: You shall not do injustice in judgment, in measures of length, in weight, and in measures of volume.

R.35: Be fair and honest when you judge. Be honest when you measure how long something is, how much it weighs, or how much it holds.

decisions.choice: in judgment, in measurement, in weight, in measure: in courts and in trade alike
decisions.reason: "Judgment" repeats the start of verse 15 and may here also cover any decision about what is due. The other three words name measures of length, weight and volume (Ezekiel 4:11, 16). The same God who requires justice in court requires it in the market (Deuteronomy 25:13-16; Proverbs 11:1; Amos 8:5).

records.source: מֹ֧אזְנֵי צֶ֣דֶק אַבְנֵי־צֶ֗דֶק אֵ֥יפַת צֶ֛דֶק וְהִ֥ין צֶ֖דֶק יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־הוֹצֵ֥אתִי אֶתְכֶ֖ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Balances of righteousness, weights of righteousness, [an] ephah of righteousness, and [a] hin of righteousness will be to you; I [am] Yahweh your God, who brought out you from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: Keep scales that are true and weights that are true, and a true dry measure ({{units:about 20 quarts|an ephah}}) and a true liquid measure ({{units:about a gallon|a hin}}). I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

L.36: Righteous scales, righteous weights, a righteous ephah, and a righteous hin you shall have; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

R.36: Your scales and your weights must be honest. Your measures for grain ({{units:about 20 quarts|an ephah}}) and for liquids ({{units:about a gallon|a hin}}) must be honest too. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. I brought you out of Egypt.

decisions.choice: balances and weights: scales with stones used to weigh goods and silver
decisions.reason: Goods and money were weighed on a pair of scales against stones of fixed weight. A trader could cheat by keeping one set of stones for buying and a lighter set for selling (Deuteronomy 25:13-15; Proverbs 20:10; Micah 6:11).

decisions.choice: ephah and hin: the standard measures for dry goods and for liquids
decisions.reason: The ephah was a dry measure for grain and flour, a little over half a bushel; its tenth part is the measure of flour in many offerings (5:11). The hin was a liquid measure for oil and wine, about a gallon (23:13; Numbers 15:4-10). Both figures are approximate; the exact sizes are not known and may have varied.

decisions.choice: of righteousness: accurate, true to the standard
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 15. Used of scales and measures it means right, honest, matching the true standard (Deuteronomy 25:15; Ezekiel 45:10).

decisions.choice: who brought you out of the land of Egypt: the God who set Israel free requires justice
decisions.reason: The LORD who rescued Israel from oppression in Egypt (Exodus 20:2) will not have them cheat one another. The words close the chapter's laws, as they close the laws of 11:45 and 22:33.

decisions.choice: true (Balanced); honest (Readable)
decisions.reason: Used of scales and measures, "righteous" means accurate. Literal keeps "righteous" so that the link with verse 15 shows.

decisions.choice: a true dry measure (about 20 quarts) ... a true liquid measure (about a gallon)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the kind of measure and give its modern size; the Measures setting shows "an ephah" and "a hin". A tenth of an ephah is about 2 quarts (5:11). Literal keeps the Hebrew units.

records.source: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־כָּל־חֻקֹּתַי֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־מִשְׁפָּטַ֔י וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And you will keep all my statutes and all my judgments, and you will do them; I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: Keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} rulings, and put them into practice. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

L.37: And you shall keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} statutes and all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} judgments, and do them; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

R.37: Obey all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} laws and rules. Do what they say. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

decisions.choice: keep all my statutes and judgments, and do them: the closing call to obey
decisions.reason: The chapter ends as chapter 18 does (18:4-5, 26), by calling for obedience to all God's laws. "Keep" and "do" together mean to guard the commands and to carry them out. The words statutes and judgments are explained at 18:4. The speech that began in verse 2 ends here.
